key_insight: Levi--Civita coordinates stabilize close-encounter orbital dynamics dramatically better than Cartesian coordinates, but they make neural residual learning harder in raw feature space.
engineering_relevance: For high-eccentricity Hamiltonian simulation, regularization can greatly improve rollout robustness and energy conservation, yet the coordinate choice can create optimization bottlenecks for learned models.
method: Compared Cartesian vs. planar Levi--Civita formulations on a perturbed Kepler system with an analytic quadrupole potential.
Evaluated Hamiltonian splitting, matched physical horizon/force budget, held-out high-eccentricity rollouts, and neural residual fitting.
Used exact-feature controls, least-squares fits, and orthogonalization to isolate dynamical versus optimization effects.
evidence_signal: At eccentricities up to 0.99, Levi--Civita kept max relative energy error near 2.1×10^-5 and produced 40/40 finite high-eccentricity rollouts, while Cartesian became unstable and failed all 40/40 tests.
watch_item: The regularized setup supplies exact initial orbit energy and still leaves O(1) residual error in surviving neural rollouts, so the result is a conditioning trade-off rather than a solved learning pipeline.
paper_title: Dynamical and Optimization Trade-offs of Levi--Civita Coordinates for Learned Close-Encounter Dynamics
